narrative: The model estimated an 84% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, so your application was denied because the computer judged you substantially more likely than a typical applicant to miss repayments. The strongest factor was your checking-account position: your account is overdrawn, shown as below zero DM. That is uncommon among approved applicants—most have no overdraft or a positive balance—so it pushed the decision toward bad credit. The second-strongest factor was the requested repayment period of 60 months, far longer than the approved average of about 19 months. A long loan term increases uncertainty and made the prediction riskier. Third was that your property or collateral position is recorded as unknown or none; only about 8% of approved applicants have that profile, so this also pushed toward denial. These three factors outweighed the strengths in your profile, such as long employment and stable housing. To improve your chances, ask the lender which information can be corrected or added, especially property or collateral details. Consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter repayment period, providing a guarantor or co-applicant, and bringing your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying.
